verdict.rationale: ROS 2 is open-source software that users install and run on their own machines. The official Ubuntu deb install docs offer ROS-Base and Desktop variants plus a verification step, and community sources confirm it is open source. A practitioner notes the Open Robotics debs aren't suitable for most product deployments, which is a packaging caveat rather than a contradiction of self-hosting. Missing for 10: an explicit license statement in the evidence, build-from-source or non-Ubuntu install documentation, and production deployment guidance.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: ROS-Base Install (Bare Bones): Communication libraries, message packages, command line tools. No GUI tools.
Desktop Install (Recommended): ROS, RViz, demos, tutorials.
This verifies both the C++ and Python APIs are working properly.
being open source means everyone can improve it
